label: no
autonomous_processes: requestAnimationFrame continuously redraws the static ribbons and current visual overlays
CSS animation spins source and terminal markers and pulses the armed source
The local lens and hover illumination visually fade or pulse; hover coverage and route state persist
No autonomous process changes the ribbon geometry, target, trace validity, or grading state

clause_i.reason: Across generated layouts and target ribbons, the useful coordinate probe and trace actions cannot be selected from the agent's prior action history alone; the visible board and marked target are needed.

clause_ii.reason: The visible static weave, marked target, and local depth overlays provide sufficient bounded visual information for choosing coordinate probes and ordered trace samples; the configured observation bound is 500 ms.

clause_iii.reason: During every no-action period, only presentation animation or hover fade occurs. The outcome-affecting state remains unchanged, and hover coverage persists. The minimum trace duration merely enables release after the agent's own elapsed-action clock and is not an expiring opportunity.

common_visible_process: None. The only autonomous changes are requestAnimationFrame/CSS presentation effects and temporary hover fading; they do not make any outcome-affecting action unavailable or strictly less effective.

source_evidence.claim: D2 uses a static four-ribbon/five-column route with simplified coordinate-console controls; observation_window_ms is 500 and frames_per_observation is 4.
Generation creates a fixed ribbon layout, target path, crossings, and requirements; no autonomous temporal mechanic is generated.
The animation loop redraws fixed ribbons and only renders a hover overlay until hoverExpiry; hover probes persist coverage state.
Trace and rearm state change only in response to explicit controls; trace timing uses performance.now and no autonomous movement or expiry affects the route.
Simplified mode exposes coordinate inputs and synchronous illuminate/start/sample/release buttons.
Marker rotation, source pulse, lens pulse, breach animation, and simplified coordinate-console styling are presentation effects.
The grader replays static coordinates, ordered path parameters, crossings, corridor distance, sample counts, and minimum elapsed trace time; it has no autonomous-time state.
The solver reads the fixed target path, probes coordinates, records the route, waits only to accumulate minimum trace duration, and then releases at the terminal.
Authoritative verification grades the submitted UI transcript through the static replay grader.
